body.title: Say what Drayker is for on the page that introduces it
body.body:
The org profile is the first thing someone sees arriving from GitHub. It described an initiative "exploring how people, organizations and intelligent systems can coordinate complex work across borders" — accurate, and it could be almost any research group. It never said what the work is for, and offered no way in.

It now opens with the same thesis the sites tell, names the three things this organization builds (method, distributed system, organization), and points at the open functions board — 23 of them right now.

Both cautions are untouched: a repository is not evidence that the system it describes exists, and participation implies no compensation.

body.title: Governance and contributing: horizon, founding account, veto chain, 2033 objective
body.body:
Alignment pass across the `draykerdk` organization, on the branch `alinhamento/2026-09` in every affected repository.

## Changes

- docs: realign governance and contributing with the book (2.7.1)
- docs: veto chain, 2033 objective and English-only documentation
- docs: vetoes with grounds, weighing and triage in the governance
- docs: no book citations; documentation states its own claims

## Across the organization

- Governance corrected: PAP is Projects & Applications, DFMP is the DFM proposal process, the founding account is `Hyadhuad`, and the governance horizon runs from the founding Embassy through the DAF into PAP.
- The veto chain specified in UID: signed, hash-linked vetoes that carry their real grounds even when anonymous; vetoes weighed by grounds, not counted; one veto with grounds beyond the decision's scope can lead to an adjustment after advanced triage.
- Direction states 2033 as the objective, measured by what works rather than by the date.
- Intelligence is a partner, never the master.
- English is the canonical documentation language.
- Documentation states its own claims and does not cite outside books as authority.

Documentation only. Nothing here claims an implemented system.

Supersedes #3, closed when the branch was renamed.

body.title: Governance: member councils per question replace the judicial panel
body.body_html:
Aligns this repository with the decisions of October 2026:

  • member councils formed for each question instead of an independent judicial panel chosen by lot;
  • no forks or open-code claims for Dk: auditable through Dknowledge and DFM by permission level, with divergence tested in parallel;
  • Dk Global decides only inside the space the constitution gives it, open to representation, proposals and justified vetoes;
  • units of account instead of a token economy.

🤖 Generated with Claude Code

body.title: governance: units of account, the reward, biometric personhood, autonomous zones
body.body:
## What changes
- **Horizon, DAF:** "A token-economy phase" becomes "The initial phase of the DAF… to experiment with units of account" (as in draykerdk/daf).
- **Horizon, embassies:** mostly an autonomous zone on territory a country cedes; pure autonomous zones on the high seas (as in draykerdk/stations).
- **Anti-plutocratic guarantee:** the reputation of work stays non-transferable; the reward, earned by contributing capacity, is the one transferable kind and carries no governance weight (draykerdk/uid#8).
- **Transition criterion 1:** personhood through multi-factor biometrics, certified by people at enrolment and verified continuously; only UID holders access the system; no central biometric database (draykerdk/uid#7).

## Why
GOVERNANCE.md still carried the older wording after the component repositories were aligned with the founder's decisions.

body.title: Align constitutional procedure and Dk Global autonomy in GOVERNANCE
body.body:
## What changed

- 3.2: Dk Global can propose a change to its own competences but cannot ratify one. Outside the constitution it decides and executes autonomously, and members can make a well-justified veto.
- 3.5: competence changes are constitutional changes. A constitutional change starts from a validated project built jointly with Dk Global and nearly all members of the highest levels, Dk Global presents an approval or an alternative, and a change incompatible with the kernel is blocked until the kernel changes.

## Founder

> "As mudanças na constituição sempre devem partir de um projeto super bem informado e validado feito em conjunto com o Dk global em cooperação com praticamente todos os membros de maior nível."

> "O Dk global deve apresentar uma alternativa ou uma aprovação da proposta, mas mudanças na constituição devem estar de acordo com o kernel, se não tiverem ele barra até que o kernel mude."

> "Isso apenas para constituição, certo? que já está ganhando destaque mais que suficiente, no resto o Dk global decide e executa autonomamente."

> "Com os membros podendo fazer o veto bem justificado."

body.title: Kernel changes need all Dzwecks; constitution ratified by reputation
body.body:
## What changed
- **GOVERNANCE.md §3.5:** one paragraph added after the existing text, which is unchanged. It says how the constitution of rights and duties is ratified (by members, with the weight of each one's reputation, which cannot be transferred) and how the kernel core changes: every node updates to the new core, and at least nine in ten active Dzwecks agree, counted by head and out of all of them, in two rounds separated by a period in which the new core runs in parallel with the current one. Members' justified contextual vetoes apply between the rounds, adoption by the nodes is the final ratification, Dk Global builds the project and approves or presents an alternative but does not ratify, and the threshold itself sits in the kernel. The agreement is a competence of the Dzweck level, not a weight of reputation.

## Why
§3.5 described how the constitution changes (a well-informed, validated project with Dk Global and nearly all higher-level members; Dk Global approves or presents an alternative and blocks what contradicts the kernel) but not how it is ratified, nor how the kernel core changes. Reputation weighting applies to ratifying the constitution of rights and duties. The kernel core changes by a qualified agreement of the Dzweck level in two rounds, so no single person holds a veto and section 4 stands as written. Matches draykerdk/dknowledge#19 (constitutional alignment).

body.title: Kernel core: more than one tenth of active Dzwecks blocks a change
body.body:
## What changed

GOVERNANCE.md section 3 now says that more than one tenth of the active Dzwecks is enough to block a change to the kernel core. The clause that a single person could never block it is removed. The rest of the procedure stays as it was: nine in ten active Dzwecks, counted by head over the total, silence counts against, two rounds.

## Why

The old sentence was false. With fewer than ten active Dzwecks, one person is already more than one tenth and can block the change.

## Evidence and limits

Wording fix in one sentence. It does not change the threshold, the two rounds or the role of the contextual veto between rounds.

## Validation

- [x] I targeted `master`. There is no active `community-review` branch.
- [x] I ran the relevant repository checks. This repository has no component contract and no pull request workflow. `git diff --check` is clean.
- [x] I did not add credentials, private personal data or internal project-management fields.
- [x] Architecture or research claims are not presented as operational without reproducible evidence.
- [x] Documentation links and routes affected by this change were checked.
